no REST trigger · first ingest, re-ingest and replay are one code path

g.data-name: lane:The corpus · three databases, and the evidence behind them
g.text: THE CORPUS · THREE DATABASES, AND THE EVIDENCE BEHIND THEM
one writer per store, arrived at by removing a violation

g.data-name: lane:Verification · asked and answered after every ingest
g.text: VERIFICATION · ASKED AND ANSWERED AFTER EVERY INGEST
observer only · changes no version, chunk, vector or edge

g.data-name: lane:Pipeline B · query — a question answered from the stored corpus
g.text: PIPELINE B · QUERY — A QUESTION ANSWERED FROM THE STORED CORPUS
nothing here writes a store, and nothing here parses a law
LEGAL KNOWLEDGE DATABASE · THE WHOLE SYSTEM
Pipeline A ingests the law, proves it, and stores it. Pipeline B answers questions from it. A writes every store; B writes none — which is why a retrieval bug cannot corrupt the corpus, and
why a question cannot trigger a re-ingest.

g.data-name: card:Fourteen gates, run by the ingest
g.text: Fourteen gates, run by the ingest
Publishing law.embedded is what runs them — nobody asks. They cover structural fidelity,
citation correctness, cross-store equality and source currency, and the verdict is never one

text.font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "Cascadia Code", Consolas, "SF Mono", Menlo, monospace

g.data-name: card:A denominator that cannot share the defect
g.text: A denominator that cannot share the defect
The structural inventory is read a second time on a different XML stack, importing no
parser code. And the prover proves itself first: if an already-certified law stops reproducing
under today's rules, no law gets a verdict — including the one being certified.

g.text: WHERE THE DE AND EU ANSWERS DIFFER
Two of the fourteen are structurally inapplicable to EU sources, and
both say so in code with a named reason rather than silently not
EU acts parse, ingest and are queryable, but no EU law is certified:
the end-to-end assurance contract does not exist yet, so the prover
returns INCONCLUSIVE for a FORMEX law. A missing contract, not
The two pipelines share one corpus and nothing else. Every component in A writes exactly one store and the write arrows above are the only writes
that exist; every component in B reads and returns. That separation is why a retrieval bug cannot corrupt the corpus, and why a question cannot start
It is also why B has no verification gate of its own and needs none. B trusts the corpus because A proved it before it was served.
Three limits worth stating with the rest. There is no dead-letter topic on this pipeline, so a permanently unprocessable law is redelivered for ever and
blocks its partition until a human intervenes.
The chatbot and the LLM are existing components whose repositories are outside the audited workspace, so no internal detail of them is drawn. And
validating each cited section against the corpus before an answer is shown — the check that would catch a hallucinated citation — is a design position
